proposal.root_cause: Commit 1b30a6794b56bff79300d57b7510380a2ef91805 added an env var WORKER_TOKEN referencing secretKeyRef worker-credentials/WORKER_TOKEN, while the Secret it defined (and that exists in the cluster) only contains key WORKER_ID, so kubelet fails with CreateContainerConfigError and the pod stays Pending.
proposal.rationale: Pod worker-554ff6d46f-69dgt is Pending with CreateContainerConfigError: "couldn't find key WORKER_TOKEN in Secret demo/worker-credentials". The cluster Secret worker-credentials only has key WORKER_ID (confirmed via k8s_list secrets). Git history shows commit 1b30a6794b56bff79300d57b7510380a2ef91805 ("chore(demo): update worker.yaml") introduced BOTH the env var WORKER_TOKEN -> secretKeyRef(worker-credentials, WORKER_TOKEN) AND the Secret definition containing only WORKER_ID — a self-inconsistent change that is the root cause. The last known-good pod template (running ReplicaSet worker-65d89fdfc8, pod worker-65d89fdfc8-ddjbl Ready 1/1, and worker.yaml at parent commit daa020ab) has no env block at all. No WORKER_TOKEN value exists anywhere in git or cluster evidence, so the grounded minimal fix is to remove the env block, restoring the last known-good template. The Secret object added by the same commit is harmless and left untouched to keep the change minimal.
proposal.verify: After Argo CD syncs the patch, a new worker ReplicaSet/pod is created whose template matches the previously running worker-65d89fdfc8 template (no WORKER_TOKEN env); the pod should leave Pending, reach Running/Ready 1/1 with restarts=0, and no CreateContainerConfigError events should appear.
